source_citation: Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center, University of Texas at Austin, Native Plant Database, Bauhinia lunarioides; record modified 2026-09-30
source_name: Bauhinia lunarioides A. Gray ex S. Watson

morphology_source_reported.growth_habit: Deciduous perennial, single- or multi-stemmed shrub or small tree, 6–12 feet high
morphology_source_reported.flowers: White to pale pink, orchid-like and fragrant, clustered with projecting stamens

habitat_source_reported: Limestone-hill canyons and arroyos; well-drained substrates; cited in Kinney, Presidio, and Gillespie or Llano counties
flowering_source_reported: Mar–May, sometimes again after heavy summer or fall rain
